profile.campus: Santa Clara, Santa Clara County, California (Microsoft 'BY1-2' data center retrofit, Silicon Valley)
profile.address: 2055 Lafayette Street, Santa Clara, Santa Clara County, California, 95050
profile.reading:
This building at 2055 Lafayette Street in Santa Clara matches the site of what engineering firm BKF Engineers describes as Microsoft's "BY1-2" data center retrofit project, spanning 2045 and 2055 Lafayette Street. BKF, which managed civil engineering, construction management, permitting, stormwater systems, surveying, and utility coordination for the project, described it as transforming a decommissioned facility into a modern, high-capacity data center: a 35.2-megawatt, two-story building comprising two 17.6-megawatt sections, BY1 and BY2, connected by a central electrical room. The retrofit required careful sequencing because certain IT racks and supporting equipment remained live and in service during demolition and reconstruction elsewhere in the building, requiring safety protocols to maintain uninterrupted operation throughout. Microsoft has continued expanding its wider Silicon Valley footprint beyond this retrofit: Data Center Dynamics reported the company purchased 64.5 acres of additional Silicon Valley land while considering a large new data center, and a related project was reported approved by the San Jose Planning Commission. Microsoft's own local.microsoft.com site publishes a California community page and a dedicated "Microsoft datacenters in California" fact sheet, though consistent with its general disclosure practice it does not itemize exact per-building specs there. This Lafayette Street facility's 35.2MW total and 17.6MW-per-section figures, from BKF's own project description, are among the more specific building-level capacity figures found anywhere in this registry for a Microsoft facility, since BKF worked directly on the retrofit rather than relying on aggregator estimates.

Silicon Valley Power, Santa Clara's municipally owned electric utility, supplies power to the city's dense concentration of data centers including Microsoft's Lafayette Street site, and has periodically flagged capacity constraints on its distribution system as a factor data center developers must plan around, a dynamic distinct from investor-owned-utility markets elsewhere in California.

reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish capacity figures for individual data center campuses. The company discloses only aggregate worldwide statistics, stating that it operates 500+ datacenters across 80+ Azure regions but does not reveal exact addresses, square footage, or megawatt capacity for specific facilities. This Santa Clara campus on Lafayette Street is confirmed as a Microsoft data center location within the Silicon Valley footprint, but its power draw and rack count remain undisclosed.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities in this registry, but only 11 have published capacity figures totaling 365 MW. This campus cannot be ranked within California's published capacity because Microsoft does not disclose its individual site power. The absence of a published figure means this facility does not contribute to the state's known AI infrastructure baseline, regardless of its actual scale.

For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the undisclosed capacity is the operative fact. Media reports indicate Microsoft considered this Silicon Valley location for a large data center purchase, but without published specifications, its role in AI compute availability cannot be quantified against published regional or national supply. The gap is by design: Microsoft's disclosure policy makes individual campus capacity invisible to public tracking of grid constraints on AI deployment.
